en: Tap a bar to pick a cipher letter. Counting is free.
English, lined up at the wheel's setting
Tap a pair or triple to see it on the page. English leans on TH, HE and THE.
Slide the crib along the letters (spaces ignored). A cross marks a letter that contradicts itself.
Its letters agree with each other here. That's a candidate, not proof.
Rusted: every notch you turn costs Thirst.
Factor tray: how many spacings each number divides
Hold a letter on the page. If it sits in a repeat of three or more letters the lens will measure it.
Key size %d: %.2f differing bits per byte
The shortest tooth is the key size or a multiple of it. Prefer the smallest size that is nearly as short.
Average differing bits per byte between neighbouring blocks (shorter is better)
Kett: "Drag the outer ring with your thumb. The red letters are what they wrote. The black ones are what they meant."
Kett: "Count first. Tall bars are loud letters. English shouts E, T and A."
Kett: "Drag a red tile into the slot of the letter you think it hides. Hold a slot to lock a sure one."
Kett: "One wheel per tooth of the key. Drag each drum up or down."
Kett: "Hold a letter on the page. Repeats sit a multiple of the key's length apart, the lazy bastards."
Kett: "Slide N. When the strands are each plain English shifted, the vial runs red and thick."
Kett: "Tap a bead to flip it. Dark is one, pale is nought. The chalice mixes two strands."
Kett: "Turn the dial. Watch the gauge, not your hopes."
Kett: "Short tooth, likely key size. Tap it."
Kett: "Drag a word you think is in one letter. If the other letter turns to sense beneath it, you've guessed right."
Those words belong to the other letter. Pinned there.
